title: OpenQuestSpec Document (0.1-draft)
description: The normative schema for an OpenQuestSpec quest document. Structural validity is defined entirely by this schema; two semantic rules (SEM-1, SEM-2) sit outside it and are described in SPECIFICATION.md. DRAFT: no compatibility is promised between draft versions.

openquest.description: The specification version this document targets. A validator that does not know this version must reject the document rather than guess.

quests.description: Quests, keyed by id. Keys are ids, not extension fields (ADR-0011).

^x-.description: Vendor extension. Contents are unconstrained and are never interpreted by the toolchain (ADR-0010).

id.$comment: Expressed as pattern + not/pattern rather than a negative lookahead, so that validators built on RE2 (which has no lookahead) can compile it. Portability is the premise of this schema being normative.
id.description: An authored identifier: kebab-case, and not beginning with 'x-'. The 'x-' exclusion keeps id space and extension space from colliding if a future version permits extensions on a keyed map.

typeName.description: An objective or reward type. Deliberately an open string: v0.1 defines no vocabulary, so adding a type requires no schema change. A vendor segment is recommended for custom types, e.g. 'arcticflame-escort'.

params.description: Type-specific data (ADR-0012). Contents are unconstrained in 0.1-draft because no type vocabulary is defined yet; later versions add conditional validation per type. Distinct from 'x-': params is spec territory the toolchain will interpret, 'x-' is vendor territory it never will.

info.description: Document metadata. Note this object permits no 'x-' extensions: ADR-0010 allows them at the document root, quest, objective, and reward only.

title.description: Human-readable name for this document, e.g. 'Riverwood Main Questline'.

version.description: The version of this content. Unrelated to 'openquest', which is the specification version.

description.description: Authored intent for the document as a whole. JSON has no comments, so description fields are the only sanctioned place for it (ADR-0002).
Authored intent: why this quest exists, for the next designer to read.

objectives.description: Objectives, keyed by id. Unordered: objectives form a dependency graph via 'requires', not a sequence.

rewards.description: Granted when the quest completes. An array rather than a keyed map because rewards carry no identity that anything references (ADR-0011).

title.description: Player-facing label, e.g. as shown in a quest log.

description.description: Authored intent, for designers rather than players.

requires.description: Ids of objectives in the SAME quest that must complete first. Cross-quest references are not allocated in 0.1-draft. Validating that these ids resolve is SEM-1; that the resulting graph is acyclic is SEM-2. Neither is expressible in JSON Schema.
